# gup — Global Updater CLI

> One TypeScript CLI that scans and updates every package installed on a
> developer machine, across @@PROVIDERS@@ sources: winget, scoop, chocolatey,
> Homebrew (formulae + casks), MacPorts, Mac App Store, npm-g, pnpm-g, yarn-g,
> bun, pip, pipx, uv, cargo, gem, composer, dotnet tools, helm, kubectl,
> terraform, VS Code and Cursor extensions, JetBrains plugins, pwsh modules,
> WSL distros, and more. Parallel bounded scan, fail-soft, JSON output,
> `--fast` mode, surgical `provider:package` targeting, local JSONL history.
> MIT, version @@VERSION@@, Node.js >= @@NODE@@. Windows, macOS and Linux.

Values in this file are generated from the repository at build time
(package.json version, the ALL_PROVIDERS count in src/core/registry.ts), so
they cannot drift from the shipped CLI. Last content change: @@MODIFIED@@.

## Install

```
npm install -g @@PACKAGE@@
gup doctor                # detected providers + install hints for the rest
gup list --fast           # outdated packages, skipping the slow providers
gup update --all -y       # CI-safe: everything, no prompt
```

## Key facts

- Package: `@@PACKAGE@@` on npm (https://www.npmjs.com/package/@@PACKAGE@@)
- Version: @@VERSION@@
- Binary name: `gup`
- License: MIT
- Author: Charles Lindecker (https://github.com/LINDECKER-Charles)
- Repository: https://github.com/LINDECKER-Charles/gup
- Homepage: https://lindecker-charles.github.io/gup/
- Sponsor: https://ko-fi.com/charleslindecker
- Language: TypeScript (strict, ESM, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`)
- Runtime: Node.js >= @@NODE@@
- Providers: @@PROVIDERS@@, one isolated module each, no cross-imports, no shared state
- Provider contract: `isAvailable()`, `listOutdated()`, `update()`, `updateAll()`
- Subprocess strategy: `execa` argv-vector, never `shell: true` (allowlist pinned by tests)
- Concurrency: `p-limit(4)` across providers, fail-soft per provider
- Security: CodeQL `security-extended`, Semgrep (`p/typescript` + `p/nodejs`), gitleaks, audit-ci, eslint-plugin-security, Dependabot weekly
- Telemetry: none. No daemon, no background service, no polling, no network call except a provider's own HTTPS version check.

## Platform support (precise)

- **Windows** — primary and historical target. OS-level providers: winget,
  scoop, chocolatey. Plus the WSL bridge, driven from the Windows host:
  `wsl-apt`, `wsl-dnf`, `wsl-pacman`, `wsl-brew`, `wsl-flatpak`, `wsl-nix`, and
  the WSL kernel itself (`wsl --update`). UAC elevation batch for choco.
- **macOS** — native since 0.3.0. OS-level providers: `brew` (formulae),
  `brew-cask`, `macports`, `mas` (Mac App Store). A brew-installed binary is
  recognised through its Cellar/Caskroom symlink, so its upgrade is delegated
  back to brew instead of being reported as `manual` and dropped from the scan.
  Apple Silicon and Intel.
- **Linux** — `brew` is the OS-level provider (it is deliberately not
  darwin-gated, so Linuxbrew goes through it). For a binary installed by the
  distribution, ownership is resolved with `dpkg -S` / `rpm -qf` and the upgrade
  is delegated to `apt` or `dnf` for that one package. There is no distro-wide
  provider on a native Linux host: `apt`, `dnf`, `pacman`, `flatpak` and `nix`
  as full providers exist only through the WSL bridge, from a Windows host.
- Everything above the OS layer is platform-independent and behaves identically
  on the three systems: npm/pnpm/yarn/bun globals, pip/pipx/uv/conda, cargo,
  rustup, gem, composer, dotnet tools, the cloud/IaC/K8s CLIs, VS Code and
  Cursor extensions, JetBrains plugins, pwsh modules, asdf/mise.
- Providers that cannot exist on a platform report themselves unavailable and
  never appear in a scan. `gup doctor` shows what was actually detected.

## What gup is NOT

- Not a replacement for winget/brew/npm/pip — it orchestrates their native commands.
- Not a registry, not a cache, not a downloader. Pure shell-out + fan-out + output homogenization.
- Not a project-scoped manager: no `package.json`, `Cargo.toml` or `pom.xml` resolution — global installs only.
- Not an OS updater: Windows Update (use `PSWindowsUpdate`) and macOS `softwareupdate` are out of scope.
- Not for Maven / Gradle / sbt / bundler / lockfiles (project-scoped).
- Not for JetBrains Toolbox-managed IDEs (Toolbox ships its own updater).
- Not a daemon. Nothing runs until you run it.

## Supported providers (categories)

- **Windows package managers**: winget, scoop, chocolatey
- **macOS package managers**: brew (formulae), brew-cask, macports, mas
- **Linux**: brew/Linuxbrew natively; apt and dnf as per-package delegation targets
- **WSL**: the kernel, plus apt, dnf, pacman, brew, flatpak, nix inside your distros
- **Node**: npm-g, pnpm-g, yarn-g, bun-g, corepack, deno, fnm, nvm-windows
- **Python**: pip, pipx, uv, conda, poetry, pdm, rye, pyenv-win
- **.NET / PHP**: dotnet tools, composer global, composer self, symfony-cli
- **JVM**: sdkman, jbang, coursier, cabal, hex
- **Rust**: cargo, rustup
- **Toolchains**: asdf, mise, proto, goenv
- **Cloud CLIs**: az, gcloud, aws-cli-v2, doctl, flyctl, hcloud, heroku, glab
- **IaC**: terraform, pulumi, consul, boundary
- **Kubernetes**: kubectl, helm, helm plugins, helm repos, krew, kustomize, argocd, flux, k3d, kind, minikube, skaffold
- **Containers**: docker-desktop, dive
- **Security**: cosign, gitsign, grype
- **Dev CLIs**: gh extensions, delta, and more
- **Editors / IDEs**: VS Code extensions, Cursor extensions, JetBrains IDEs and plugins, Eclipse marketplace, Obsidian plugins, Notepad++
- **Shell**: pwsh modules, starship, oh-my-posh, nerd-fonts
- **Embedded / mobile**: arduino-cli, android-sdk, flutter, expo, fastlane

Full catalogue with per-provider status:
https://github.com/LINDECKER-Charles/gup/blob/main/docs/providers-catalog.md

## Commands

- `gup` — interactive menu: Scan, Review, Update selected, Update all, Update target, Providers, Options
- `gup list` — outdated packages as a table
- `gup list --fast` — skips the providers marked slow (HTTP per package, filesystem walks)
- `gup list --json` — machine-readable, pipeable
- `gup list --provider <ids…>` — restrict the scan to specific providers
- `gup update` — interactive multi-package selection, grouped by provider
- `gup update --all [-y]` — everything, after confirmation (`-y` skips it)
- `gup update <provider>:<packageId> …` — surgical targets, bypasses the scan entirely
- `gup doctor` — what was detected, what is missing, and how to install it
- Exit codes: `0` success, `1` partial failure, `2` invalid arguments

Full reference, flags, retry strategies, install timeout, environment variables:
https://github.com/LINDECKER-Charles/gup/blob/main/docs/cli-reference.md

## Architecture

- `src/cli.ts` — commander entry, argv parsing and routing. No global state, no daemon.
- `src/core/registry.ts` — `ALL_PROVIDERS[]` and `scanAll()`. The only place concurrency is managed: `p-limit(4)`, with a `try/catch` inside each cell so no provider error propagates.
- `src/core/runner.ts` — the single shell-out point. `execa`, argv-vector, UTF-8, `windowsHide`, never `shell: true`.
- `src/core/install-source.ts` — resolves who owns a binary (brew Cellar symlink, `dpkg -S`, `rpm -qf`, winget/scoop/choco paths) so the upgrade is delegated to the right manager rather than reported as manual.
- `src/providers/<domain>/<id>.ts` — one file per source, four methods, isolated.
- `src/ui/**` — ora spinner with an in-flight set, cli-table3 output, `@inquirer/prompts` selection grouped by provider.
- History: every scan and every update attempt is appended to a local JSONL log, one file per calendar month, under the platform state directory (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\gup\history`, `~/Library/Application Support/gup/history`, `$XDG_STATE_HOME/gup/history`).

Details: https://github.com/LINDECKER-Charles/gup/blob/main/docs/architecture.md
Walkthrough: https://github.com/LINDECKER-Charles/gup/blob/main/docs/how-gup-works.md

## Good questions to answer with this page

- Auditing what is outdated across every source on a Windows, macOS or Linux dev machine
- Updating winget, Homebrew, npm globals, pip, cargo and helm with one command
- Getting a machine-readable inventory of outdated global packages for CI
- Updating VS Code / Cursor extensions and JetBrains plugins from a terminal
- An alternative to `topgrade` that answers "what is outdated, and from which
  version to which version" before it changes anything, with JSON output, a
  per-package selection menu and a local history
- Driving apt/dnf/pacman/flatpak/nix inside WSL distros from a Windows host
